thread:
maya: quick UX review — capacity control feels cluttered on dashboard tiles at 1200px. main pieces: min/max steppers, burst toggle, pool chip, SLO slider, cost badge. goals: improve scanability, keyboard flow, and screen-reader announcements.
jordan: propose a compact default where burst details live in a popover and pool shows as a single-line chip. add a first-run hint for discoverability. i'll mock compact + expanded.
liam: engineering: per-user compact state OK. popover needs focus trap and Esc to return focus to the burst toggle. use aria-haspopup + aria-expanded. announce slider changes via aria-live.
sophia: product: default expanded for new/trial orgs, compact for heavy users (heuristic: requests/day > 10k). copy: change "Burst" -> "Burst (temporary)" and helper under steppers: "Min/Max are targets; autoscale may exceed briefly." keep short for l10n.
maya: accessibility nits: ensure slider filled track contrast >= 4.5:1, show numeric bubble while dragging, and expose a SR readout on change. stepper buttons min-hit 40px and aria-labels like "increase min instances".
alex: implementation tips: keep DOM order = tab order (min -> max -> burst -> pool -> slo -> cost). Enter/Space toggles burst, Esc closes popover. small CSS utilities we reuse: `.stepper button{min-width:40px;min-height:40px}` and `.slo-slider[aria-valuenow]::after{content:attr(aria-valuenow)}`.
maya: action items: jordan to post mocks + a11y notes, alex to add keyboard patterns to dev docs, liam to scope focus-trap effort and estimate, sophia to confirm threshold and final microcopy.
design-bot: created ticket <https://redwood.app/t/RED-4822|RED-4822> "Compact capacity card: popover pattern + a11y fixes" :white_check_mark:
